claims.text: Generative AI models produce probabilistic and non-replicable outputs across repeated identical input prompts.
The architecture of generative AI systems within an information systems context consists of three core layers: model layer, connection layer, and application layer.

evidence.description: The authors explain that prompting a generative AI model with an identical prompt yields varying valid outputs due to inherent output variance.
The paper presents a conceptual framework mapping the model layer, connection layer, and application layer within an organizational environment.

methodologies.name: Explorative Literature Synthesis
methodologies.description: Synthesizes technical literature on deep generative models alongside empirical application examples to conceptualize core properties and challenges of generative AI.

limitations.text: The provided framework is based on qualitative literature synthesis and lacks empirical quantitative evaluation of generative AI adoption.
Automatic evaluation methods for detecting model hallucinations remain prone to errors and inferior to manual human assessment.

future_work.text: Developing measures and mechanisms to ensure technological transparency and enhance public trust in generative AI.
Formulating structured process models for deploying generative AI-based systems safely in enterprise environments.
